## **4\. Non-Functional Requirements**

### **4.1 External Interfaces**

#### ***4.1.1 User Interfaces (UI)***

The system delivers an Omnichannel Cross-Platform frontend architecture built upon the React Ecosystem (React Native for Mobile and ReactJS for Web), managed under a unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) model across Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile form factors:

**Citizen Application (React Native Mobile \- iOS/Android & ReactJS PWA/Web)**:  

Designed for extreme simplicity and high stress: One-Touch SOS trigger button prominently positioned; accessible with one hand.  

Interactive live tracking view displaying dispatched rescue vehicle location, estimated time of arrival (ETA), and mission progress.  

Clean personal medical profile management interface (blood type, emergency contacts, medical history).  

Accessible via native mobile installation or instantly via mobile/desktop web browser without installation.

**Rescue Staff Application (React Native Mobile \- Android/iOS & ReactJS Web Fallback)**:  

High-contrast, sunlight-readable UI optimized for field vehicle tablets and smartphones.  

Dedicated Mission Dashboard with large touch targets (\>= 48dp) for 1-tap operational status changes (*Accepted*, *En Route*, *On Scene*, *Completed*).  

Integrated turn-by-turn navigation overlay and on-scene digital completion report form.  

Emergency web fallback mode allowing crew members to log into any mobile/desktop browser to maintain operational communication if native hardware fails.

**Command Center Operator Console (ReactJS Web Responsive & Tablet Adaptive)**:  

Professional dispatch console optimized for dual-monitor desktop setups (Full HD 1920x1080 minimum resolution).  

Adaptive layout dynamically collapsing into swipe-up bottom sheets and marker clustering when accessed on mobile or tablet devices for on-field supervisors.  

Real-time interactive Live Map (Leaflet/Mapbox) rendering active incidents (color-coded by severity) and rescue fleet positions.  

Incident Priority Queue pane with instant visual notifications, audio alerts, and side-by-side verification view (citizen media vs. AI classification suggestions).

**System Administrator Portal (ReactJS Web Responsive)**:  

Comprehensive management interfaces for Stations, Vehicle Fleets, Equipment, User Accounts, Role-Based Access Control, and Escalation Rule configurations, fully responsive on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

#### ***4.1.2 Hardware Interfaces***

**GPS / Geolocation Sensors**: Frontend interfaces call unified hardware abstraction wrappers: invoking device native GNSS receivers (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo) via React Native Geolocation on mobile, and falling back to HTML5 Geolocation API / IP-based location on ReactJS Web.

**Camera and Microphone Modules**: Native mobile apps interface directly with camera hardware via React Native Camera; web browser clients access hardware via WebRTC MediaStream API (navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia) for video recording (up to 10 seconds) and scene photo capture.

**Audio & Haptic Feedback Hardware**: Rescue staff devices interface with vibration motors and sound subsystems to deliver urgent, distinct alert chimes (*EMERGENCY\_DISPATCH* notification channel) and high-intensity haptic vibrations that override system "Do Not Disturb" (DND) modes during urgent dispatches, avoiding disruptive continuous siren audio.

#### ***4.1.3 Software Interfaces***

**Relational Database (PostgreSQL with PostGIS)**: Managed PostgreSQL 16 database hosted on Neon Cloud; communicates via EF Core with Npgsql driver for spatial indexing and geofencing queries.

**AI Vision-Language Inference Service**: A model-agnostic multimodal inference service serving the champion Vision-Language Model fine-tuned via LoRA—empirically evaluated and selected from a benchmark pool of five candidate architectures: Qwen2.5-VL (2B/7B), Pixtral-12B-2409, InternVL3-2B, SmolVLM-Instruct (2.2B), and Llama-3.2-Vision-Instruct (11B). Hosted via a containerized vLLM/FastAPI runtime, the engine is specialized for dual-event incident classification (Fire & Explosion and Traffic Accident) across three operational severity tiers plus Level 0\. Resilient fallback integration with cloud multimodal APIs (Qwen2.5-VL via OpenRouter) guarantees continuous mission-critical service availability. 

**Cloud Media Storage (Cloudinary CDN)**: High-performance cloud media management service for securely uploading, transforming, compressing, and hosting incident photos and videos over HTTPS.

**Push Notification Service (Firebase Cloud Messaging \- FCM & Web Push API)**: Google FCM API v1 delivering low-latency background push alerts to React Native mobile devices, and Web Push API delivering browser notification pop-ups on desktop web clients.

**Mapping & Reverse Geocoding Services**: Integration with Goong Maps / OpenStreetMap (Nominatim & OSRM) for converting latitude/longitude into human-readable Vietnamese street addresses and calculating road-network routing and ETA.

#### ***4.1.4 Communications Interfaces***

**Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS)**: All client-server REST API interactions are encrypted using TLS 1.3 / TLS 1.2 over port 443 with strict CORS whitelist enforcement.

**WebSocket Protocol (WSS \- SignalR Core)**: Full-duplex persistent WebSocket connections for instant bi-directional messaging:  

Dispatch Queue updates pushed instantly to Command Center Operators.  

Real-time GPS coordinates streamed from active rescue vehicles to dispatchers and citizens every 3-5 seconds.

**Data Interchange Format**: Standard UTF-8 encoded JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) for all RESTful API request/response payloads and SignalR message bodies.

### **4.2 Quality Attributes**

This section defines the non-functional quality requirements governing the Municipal Emergency Rescue Dispatch Platform. Built in accordance with ISO/IEC 25010 and public-safety operational standards, the system mandates rigorous, quantifiable benchmarks across usability, high-availability reliability, real-time telemetry performance, strict data privacy, modular maintainability, and cross-platform omnichannel consistency. 

#### ***4.2.1 Usability*** 

**Emergency Ergonomics**: Citizens in high-stress situations must be able to transmit an SOS alert in 3 or fewer taps within 5 seconds of launching the application.

**One-Handed Operation**: Core citizen emergency reporting and staff status update buttons are placed within the natural thumb zone on mobile screens.

**Color Coding & Accessibility**: Incident severity levels use standardized international emergency colors (Level 1: Emerald Green, Level 2: Amber/Orange, Level 3: Crimson Red) plus Level 0: Purple / Yellow-striped warning badge, combined with event iconography to support color-blind dispatchers and rapid situational awareness.

**Operator Operational Efficiency**: The CAD console provides an integrated, non-blocking single-screen workflow enabling dispatchers to rapidly review AI triage suggestions, verify on-scene media, and issue dispatch orders directly from the command live map interface without page redirection.

**Bilingual Support**: All user interfaces support Vietnamese (primary) and English (secondary), switchable on runtime.

#### ***4.2.2 Reliability*** 

**System Availability (Uptime)**: Mission-critical 24/7 emergency dispatch operation targeting 99.5% uptime (maximum allowable unplanned downtime \< 43.8 hours/year).

**Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF)**: Minimum 720 continuous operating hours (30 days) without critical system-wide service disruption.

**Mean Time To Repair (MTTR)**: Maximum 15 minutes for containerized automated recovery and service restart upon fatal unhandled faults.

**AI Graceful Degradation & Fallback**: If the external AI vision inference service times out (\> 20s) or fails, the system automatically falls back to Severity Level 0 (Rejected / Re-verification Required) and immediately pushes the incident to the top of the Operator Queue alongside Level 3 with an urgent review badge. Dispatch operations never halt due to AI downtime.

**Mobile & Web Offline Queueing**: In the event of cellular or Wi-Fi network dropout, citizen SOS reports and staff completion submissions are cached in local client storage (AsyncStorage on React Native, IndexedDB on ReactJS Web) and automatically synchronized with exponential backoff upon network reconnection.

**Zero Critical Defect Rate**: No critical defects (defined as data corruption, loss of active incident tracking, or failure to trigger dispatch alerts) permitted in production releases.

#### ***4.2.3 Performance***

**SOS Submission Latency**: Citizen SOS report ingestion API response time must be \< 3.0 seconds (excluding client-side media upload duration).

**AI Inference Latency**: End-to-end multimodal classification response within \<= 20 seconds (local Pixtral-12B LoRA).

**Real-Time SignalR Broadcast**: Vehicle GPS coordinates and status changes must reach active connected clients within \< 500 milliseconds.

**Live Map Rendering**: Dashboard map component renders 100 active rescue units and 50 concurrent incidents within \< 2.0 seconds.

**Dispatch Recommendation Speed**: Nearest-available unit calculation and load-aware ranking across all active fleet units must execute in \< 1.0 second.

**System Concurrency & Throughput**: Sustained capacity of \>= 100 requests/second on the backend API and \>= 200 concurrent active WebSocket connections without performance degradation.

#### ***4.2.4 Security & Privacy***

**Authentication & Token Lifecycle**: Secure stateless authentication using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) signed with HMAC-SHA256 (minimum 256-bit secret). Access token lifespan is 15 minutes; Refresh tokens expire in 7 days and utilize single-use rotation with revocation on password change.

**Credential Storage**: User passwords hashed using BCrypt with a minimum work factor (salt rounds) of 10\. Plain-text passwords are never logged or stored.

**Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)**: Strict authorization guards on all API endpoints enforcing roles: Citizen, RescueStaff, Operator, and Admin.

**Brute-Force Account Protection**: Five (5) consecutive failed authentication attempts lock the target account for 15 minutes; security alert email dispatched to the registered address.

**Privacy & PII Protection**:

Citizen phone numbers are masked (098\*\*\*456) on dispatcher screens by default; viewing full contact numbers requires an explicit unmask action that generates an audit trail entry.

Exact GPS location and medical profile data are strictly scoped: only accessible to the active Operator and the specific Rescue Staff assigned to that active incident.

**Immutable Audit Trail**: All security-sensitive actions (incident state transitions, dispatcher overrides, role assignments, unit dispatches) are logged to an append-only audit repository.

#### ***4.2.5 Maintainability & Portability***

**Architectural Modularity**: Built upon ASP.NET Core Clean Architecture (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API) ensuring loose coupling and testability.

**Shared Codebase & Monorepo Logic**: React Native mobile app and ReactJS web console share 100% of TypeScript DTO interfaces, API client hooks, validation schemas, and state management utilities.

**Web Browser Compatibility**: Modern standards-compliant web dashboard responsive on Google Chrome (v110+), Mozilla Firefox (v110+), Microsoft Edge (v110+), and Apple Safari (v16+).

**Containerized Deployment**: Backend API and background workers packaged via Docker and orchestrated with Docker Compose for consistent staging and production deployment.

#### ***4.2.6 Cross-Platform Omnichannel Quality Attributes***

**NFR-CP-01 (Hardware & API Abstraction)**: Frontend code utilizes common abstraction adapters. For example, getLocation() calls native GPS sensors on React Native and HTML5 Geolocation on ReactJS Web; openMediaCapture() calls native camera on mobile and WebRTC webcam on desktop without application crash.

**NFR-CP-02 (Adaptive & Responsive UX)**: All user interfaces must adapt seamlessly across 3 standard breakpoints:

Mobile: \< 600px (Vertical single-column card list, bottom navigation, touch gestures).

Tablet: 600px \- 1024px (Collapsible drawer, adaptive bottom sheets, marker clustering).

Desktop: \> 1024px (Full multi-column CAD console, dual-panel live map, mouse hover/drag-and-drop).

All interactive elements enforce an ergonomic Touch Target size of at least 48x48 dp / px.

**NFR-CP-03 (Cross-Platform Rendering Performance)**:

React Native: Maintains steady 60 FPS frame rate when rendering 100 moving vehicle markers on mobile maps.

ReactJS Web: First Contentful Paint (FCP) \<= 1.5 seconds; map rendering utilizes WebGL/Canvas acceleration to prevent browser thread locking during high-frequency WebSocket streams.

**NFR-CP-04 (Unified Offline Storage)**: Seamless client persistence layer utilizing AsyncStorage on React Native and IndexedDB on ReactJS Web for caching un-synced SOS reports and map tile buffers during cellular disconnects.

**NFR-CP-05 (Single Source of Truth CI/CD):** Continuous integration pipeline builds and validates the shared TypeScript contract library, deploying web static assets to cloud hosting (Vercel/Netlify) and compiling release .apk (Android) and .ipa (iOS) packages simultaneously to prevent version drift between platforms.

#### 

## **5\. Requirement Appendix**

This appendix supplements the functional and non-functional requirements by detailing the definitive operational rules, transversal system constraints, message catalogs, and compliance standards governing the platform. It is structured into four core technical subsections: Section 5.1 specifies the catalog of 35 encoded business rules (BR-01 to BR-35); Section 5.2 outlines common engineering conventions, input validations, and response envelopes; Section 5.3 provides the standardized application message catalog (MSG01 to MSG52); and Section 5.4 details legal compliance under Decree 13/2023/ND-CP and automated disaster recovery protocols.

### **5.1 Business Rules**

| Rule ID | Business Rule Name | Rule Definition / Specification |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| **BR-01** | **Dual-Event 3-Level Incident Severity Classification** | Every verified incident is categorized into one of two primary emergency events: Fire & Explosion or Traffic Accident, and classified across 3 Severity Levels (1 to 3\) plus Level 0 (Rejected / Re-verification Required): **Domain 1: Fire & Explosion:**   *\- Level 1 (Minor / Incipient):* Small contained fires, sparse smoke, burning trash, dry grass/brush fires, or localized kitchen/electrical smoking already demarcated without risk of structural spread or immediate life hazard.   *\- Level 2 (Moderate / Spreading):* Fires in residential homes, individual apartments, commercial storefronts, or motor vehicles (cars, trucks) on roads; dense black smoke columns, vigorous active flames, and imminent danger of spreading to adjacent structures.   *\- Level 3 (Critical / Catastrophic):* Major fires or explosions in high-rise buildings, industrial warehouses, chemical factories, fuel/gas stations; accompanied by structural collapse or loud detonations; occupants trapped on upper floors or engulfed in toxic fumes posing critical mass-casualty life threats. Authorizes multi-unit dispatch (Fire Trucks \+ Ambulances). **Domain 2: Traffic Accident:**   *\- Level 1 (Minor Collision):* Low-speed scrapes or collisions between motorcycles/bicycles or minor vehicle body fender benders; vehicles operable or lightly damaged; victims sustain only superficial abrasions or mild shock with full self-mobility; no entrapment and minimal localized traffic congestion.   *\- Level 2 (Moderate / Severe Collision):* High-impact collisions between cars and motorbikes, head-on passenger car collisions, or vehicle rollovers; substantial vehicular deformation; casualties with severe trauma (fractures, active bleeding, loss of consciousness) requiring immediate emergency medical care but free of cabin/underbody entrapment; partial roadway obstruction.   *\- Level 3 (Critical / Mass-Casualty Disaster):* Multi-vehicle pileups involving high-occupancy buses, heavy transport trucks, container trucks, or hazardous fuel tankers; vehicles plunged into ravines or deep waterways; severely crushed vehicle cabins with multiple unconscious or critically injured victims deeply pinned requiring heavy hydraulic extrication cutters; active secondary fire/explosion or hazardous chemical leak hazards. Authorizes multi-unit dispatch (Ambulances \+ Heavy Rescue Units). **Level 0 (Rejected / Re-verification Required):** Assigned when the AI vision model detects no discernible emergency entity from either category (e.g., normal street scene, selfie, landscape, blurry/dark image, suspected false alarm) or when inference service errors out. The system never auto-cancels Level 0 incidents; the incident is automatically inserted at the absolute top of the Operator Queue with priority equal to Level 3 (Top Priority \- FIFO) for compulsory human re-verification to eliminate false-negative omissions. **Domain 3: Traffic Congestion:** Unlike incidents in Domain 1 (Fire & Explosion) and Domain 2 (Traffic Accident) which utilize a 3-level severity scale (Levels 1-3), traffic congestion incidents **DO NOT** use a level-based classification. The AI Vision Model exclusively performs an independent binary classification resulting in two possible states:  *\- State "Congested":* The multimedia evidence submitted by the citizen demonstrates high vehicle density, with traffic moving extremely slowly or at a complete standstill. The system automatically assigns the \#Traffic\_Jam tag and routes the incident to the Operator's priority queue for review and subsequent dispatch of traffic control units.  *\- State "Clear / Not Congested":* The multimedia evidence indicates normal traffic flow and clear roadways. The system records the absence of congestion factors and queues the report for the Operator to review and potentially reject as a false alarm or a situation not requiring official intervention. |
| **BR-02** | **Human-in-the-Loop Principle** | AI multimodal inference serves exclusively as an advisory aid. An incident cannot be dispatched to rescue teams directly by AI. A qualified Command Center Operator must review the incident, inspect the media, and confirm or override the severity rating before the incident enters the *Verified* status eligible for dispatch. |
| **BR-03** | **Severity Override Audit Justification** | When an Operator alters the severity score suggested by the AI model, the system must record both AiSuggestedSeverity and OperatorOverrideSeverity into the immutable audit trail along with a mandatory textual justification explaining the reason for the override. If an Operator downgrades a Level 3 incident to Level 1 or Level 0, a two-step confirmation dialogue is enforced. |
| **BR-04** | **Mandatory GPS & Media for SOS** | Every citizen SOS report submitted via the mobile application must contain valid GPS coordinates (latitude, longitude) and at least one (1) visual media attachment (photo or video \<= 30 seconds). Text-only SOS reports are rejected because visual media is compulsory for computer vision hazard identification and triage. |
| **BR-05** | **Citizen SOS Rate Limiting (Anti-Spam)** | A registered or anonymous citizen device is limited to submitting a maximum of 3 SOS reports within a rolling 60-minute window. Any subsequent submission within this window is throttled with an emergency message directing the caller to dial emergency phone numbers (113/114/115) directly. |
| **BR-06** | **Single Active Incident per Citizen** | A citizen is restricted to having at most one (1) active incident (status in *Pending*, *AiProcessing*, *AiProcessed*, *Verified*, *Dispatched*, *InProgress*) at any given time. A new report can only be filed after the preceding incident is marked *Completed* or *Cancelled*, preventing panic-induced duplicate submissions. |
| **BR-07** | **Proximity Duplicate Detection** | If a new SOS report is created within 200 meters of an existing active incident within a 15-minute timeframe, the system automatically flags the new report as a *Potential Duplicate*. If confirmed as duplicate by the Operator, the incident is cancelled and linked via DuplicateOfIncidentId to the parent incident for unified dispatch handling. |
| **BR-08** | **Mandatory Incident Cancellation Reason** | An incident can only be cancelled while in *Pending*, *AiProcessed*, or *Verified* status. The Operator must select a valid cancellation reason from the standardized enum: FalseReport, Duplicate, TestReport, CitizenCancelled, or Other (with mandatory explanation). Once an incident is *Dispatched*, citizen cancellation is disabled; only the Operator can terminate the mission. |
| **BR-09** | **Stale Incident Auto-Cleanup** | Any incident remaining in *Pending* or *AiProcessed* status without Operator review for longer than 24 hours is automatically cancelled by the system background worker with the reason AutoExpired\_StaleIncident. |
| **BR-10** | **Nearest-Available Dispatch Rule** | The baseline dispatch recommendation algorithm identifies all rescue units meeting three criteria: (1) Vehicle status is Available, (2) Staff account is active with zero active assignments, and (3) Current distance to incident is within search radius. Units are ranked in ascending order by straight-line Haversine distance. Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) is computed using dynamic urban speed profiles (35 km/h day, 50 km/h night). |
| **BR-11** | **Load-Aware Multi-Objective Dispatch** | To prevent depletion of emergency reserves at single stations during peak hours, the system provides a Load-Aware dispatch algorithm ranking available units by composite cost balancing distance and station capacity. |
| **BR-12** | **Dynamic Dispatch Search Radius Expansion** | The initial search radius for available rescue units is set to 10.0 kilometers. If no available units are found within this zone, the engine automatically expands the search radius by 1.5x (15.0 km, 22.5 km, up to a maximum cap of 30.0 km). If still unresolved, an immediate audio-visual alert is raised to the Operator to request inter-district mutual aid. |
| **BR-13** | **Emergency Incident-Vehicle Type Matching** | The dispatch engine enforces capability matching based on verified event type and hazard tags: Event FireExplosion prioritizes FireTruck; Level 3 automatically recommends joint dispatch with Ambulance. Event TrafficAccident prioritizes Ambulance; Level 3 automatically recommends joint dispatch with RescueTruck equipped with hydraulic extrication cutters. Incidents tagged with drowning or flood\_rescue prioritize RescueBoat. If matching vehicles are unavailable within radius, the nearest general rescue unit is proposed with an equipment warning. |
| **BR-14** | **Multi-Unit Simultaneous Dispatch** | For severe incidents classified as Level 3, the Operator is authorized to dispatch multiple rescue units simultaneously (up to 5 units, e.g., combining Fire Trucks and Ambulances). The parent incident status transitions to *Completed* only after all assigned units have submitted individual completion reports. |
| **BR-15** | **Operator Concurrent Dispatch Mutual Exclusion** | When an Operator opens an incident for verification or dispatch, the incident is placed under a 2-minute soft lock (LockedByOperatorId). Other dispatchers viewing the queue see a warning badge and cannot submit conflicting verification or dispatch commands. If two operators submit concurrently, optimistic concurrency control (RowVersion) rejects the second submission with HTTP 409 Conflict. |
| **BR-16** | **5-Minute High-Severity Escalation Rule** | If an incident with severity Level 3 or Level 0 (Reject) remains in *Pending*, *AiProcessed*, or *Dispatched* status for 5 minutes (300 seconds) without any rescue staff transitioning the assignment to *Accepted*, the background escalation daemon automatically triggers an Escalation Event: incident status changes to *Escalated*, an urgent flashing red banner appears across all Operator dashboards, and high-priority FCM push alerts are delivered to Supervisors. |
| **BR-17** | **Level 3 Catastrophic Immediate Escalation** | For catastrophic incidents rated Level 3, the initial escalation timer is shortened to 3 minutes (180 seconds). If unaccepted after 6 minutes (double timeout), a Tier-2 Super-Escalation is triggered, broadcasting urgent SMS/Email alerts to the Station Commander and all System Administrators. |
| **BR-18** | **Automatic Incident De-escalation** | When an escalated incident is accepted by a rescue staff member, the system automatically de-escalates the incident, transitioning its status from *Escalated* to *InProgress* and logging the resolution time and accepting unit in EscalationLog. |
| **BR-19** | **Off-Hours Escalation Acceleration** | During night shifts (between 22:00 and 06:00 local time), when staffing levels are reduced, all escalation timeout thresholds are automatically reduced by 50% (2.5 minutes for Level 3 and Level 0\) to ensure faster escalation during high-vulnerability periods. |
| **BR-20** | **Single Active Assignment per Staff/Vehicle** | A rescue staff member and their assigned rescue vehicle can be committed to at most one (1) active mission (status *Accepted*, *EnRoute*, or *OnScene*) at any time. A unit is excluded from the dispatch recommendation pool until their current assignment is formally completed. |
| **BR-21** | **Mission Assignment & Response Protocol** | Upon receiving an emergency dispatch alert, the assigned rescue crew leader reviews incident parameters and confirms operational response by tapping "Accept" or "Reject". Rejections require mandatory operational justification (BR-22). |
| **BR-22** | **Mandatory Assignment Rejection Justification** | If a rescue staff member explicitly rejects a dispatch assignment, they must submit a valid rejection reason: VehicleBreakdown, AlreadyOnMission, TooFar, MedicalEmergency, or Other. This event is logged in AssignmentStatusHistory for performance accountability. |
| **BR-23** | **Mandatory Continuous GPS Streaming (En Route)** | While a rescue vehicle is in *EnRoute* status, the mobile application must stream GPS updates to the server every 5 to 10 seconds. If no location heartbeat is received for more than 60 seconds, the vehicle marker on the Command Center live map displays a flashing "Signal Lost" warning. |
| **BR-24** | **Strict Assignment State Sequence Enforcement** | Mission assignments must transition strictly through the defined sequential lifecycle: Pending → Accepted → EnRoute → OnScene → Completed. Skipping intermediate operational states (e.g., jumping from *Accepted* directly to *Completed*) is rejected by the domain state machine. |
| **BR-25** | **Mandatory Completion Report with Proof** | Rescue staff cannot transition an assignment to *Completed* without submitting a digital completion report containing: (1) At least one (1) post-operation scene photograph, (2) A textual summary of actions taken, and (3) Number of casualties/victims assisted. |
| **BR-26** | **Inter-Agency Field Handover Protocol** | In cases involving casualty transfer to receiving hospitals or joint jurisdiction transfer to police/fire authorities, the rescue crew leader logs the receiving institution, contact personnel, and handover timestamp directly within the mission log for multi-agency accountability. |
| **BR-27** | **Post-Mission Vehicle Cool-Down Period** | Upon completion of an active mission, a vehicle enters an automatic 5-minute cool-down period before re-entering the Available dispatch pool. This window allows crew rest, initial equipment replenishment, and vehicle sanitization. |
| **BR-28** | **AI Vision Inference Resilience & Fallback** | The AI Vision API call is governed by a 20-second timeout with an exponential backoff retry policy (max 3 retries: 1s, 2s, 4s). If all retries fail or if the returned JSON is unparsable, the incident automatically falls back to Severity \= 0 (Unclassified), tags \["Unclassified"\], and IsSuccess \= false. The incident is immediately pushed to the top of the Operator Queue for manual human triage. |
| **BR-29** | **AI Circuit Breaker and Auto-Bypass** | If the AI vision inference service encounters 5 consecutive failures within a 2-minute sliding window, the circuit breaker opens. For the subsequent 30 seconds, all new incoming SOS reports bypass external AI calls and are routed directly to the Operator Queue with default Level 0 classification. After 30 seconds, the circuit enters a Half-Open state to test connectivity. |
| **BR-30** | **Immutable Raw AI Response Auditing** | The complete raw JSON string returned by the multimodal AI model, along with model identifier (e.g., qwen/qwen2.5-vl-72b-instruct) and token usage metrics, must be stored immutably in AiClassification.RawResponse to enable ongoing accuracy benchmarks (Precision, Recall, F1-Score). |
| **BR-31** | **Privacy-Preserving GPS and Medical Profile Access** | A citizen's exact GPS location and confidential medical profile (blood type, allergies, emergency contacts) are accessible exclusively to the active Operator handling the incident and the specific Rescue Staff assigned to that mission. Once the incident is marked *Closed*, access permissions for the staff expire immediately. |
| **BR-32** | **Masking of Citizen Personally Identifiable Information** | Citizen phone numbers are masked (098\*\*\*456) on dispatcher queue screens to safeguard personal privacy. Dispatchers may click "Reveal Phone Number" when direct verbal contact is required; clicking records an audit event capturing OperatorId, Timestamp, and IncidentId. |
| **BR-33** | **Brute-Force Account Protection** | When an account experiences five (5) consecutive failed authentication attempts, the system automatically locks the account for 15 minutes. An automated notification email with unlock instructions is dispatched to the registered address. |
| **BR-34** | **Append-Only Immutable Incident Audit Trail** | The IncidentAuditTrail table is strictly append-only. Database triggers and application repository guards prohibit SQL UPDATE and DELETE commands. Every lifecycle transition, severity override, dispatch action, and cancellation must create an immutable audit record containing actor ID, role, action enum, UTC timestamp, and state JSON snapshot. |
| **BR-35** | **Universal Soft-Delete Entity Constraint** | Critical domain entities (User, Station, Vehicle, Incident, IncidentAssignment) must utilize soft deletion (IsDeleted \= true). Physical database record deletion is forbidden to preserve complete forensic traceability and audit compliance. |

### **5.2 Common Requirements**

This section specifies the transversal engineering standards, data validation rules, communication envelopes, ergonomic constraints, and security conventions uniformly enforced across all subsystems of the Emergency Dispatch Platform, including Citizen Mobile and Progressive Web Apps, Operator Computer-Aided Dispatch Web Console, Rescue Staff Tablet, and Backend API Services.

#### 

#### ***5.2.1 Standardized API Response Envelope***

All RESTful endpoints exposed by the ASP.NET Core backend must encapsulate responses within a standardized generic envelope structure to ensure client-side determinism and uniform exception handling. A successful response contains boolean flag isSuccess set to true, HTTP status code 200, a localized descriptive message, the returned data payload, an empty errors array, a UTC timestamp, and a distributed correlation trace identifier.

In the event of validation failures or runtime exceptions, isSuccess is set to false, accompanied by corresponding HTTP 400 or 500 status codes, a human-readable error description, an array of specific field errors, and a correlation trace identifier for diagnostic logging.

#### 

#### ***5.2.2 Common Input Validation and Form Constraints***

Server-side validation strictly enforces the following domain boundaries prior to database persistence:

Telephone Numbers: Must conform to standard Vietnamese mobile telecommunications formats, consisting of exactly 10 numeric digits starting with standard prefixes such as 03, 05, 07, 08, or 09\.

Email Addresses: Must comply with official email standards, automatically normalized to lowercase, and verified for correct syntax and domain structure.

Password Complexity: Passwords require a minimum length of 8 characters and must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special character.

Citizen Identity: Exactly 12 numeric digits conforming to the Vietnamese National Citizen Identity Card standard.

Spatial Coordinates: Latitude must be strictly bounded between negative 90.0 and positive 90.0 degrees, and Longitude bounded between negative 180.0 and positive 180.0 degrees under the World Geodetic System 1984 reference standard. Geographic coordinates falling outside Vietnamese territorial boundaries automatically trigger location anomaly alerts.

Scene Media Attachments: File uploads are restricted to a maximum size of 10 Megabytes per image and 50 Megabytes per video. Audio recordings are limited to a maximum duration of 30 seconds. Supported formats include JPEG, PNG, WEBP, MP4, and AAC.

#### ***5.2.3 Security, Privacy, and Data Protection Standards***

Cryptographic Authentication: Stateless JSON Web Tokens signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a minimum 256-bit secret key. Access tokens have an expiration period of 15 minutes, while refresh tokens remain valid for 7 days with single-use rotation and client IP address binding.

Password Hashing: User passwords must be securely salted and hashed using the BCrypt algorithm with a minimum work factor of 10\. Plain-text credentials are never written to error logs, cache, or memory dumps.

Personally Identifiable Information Masking: In strict compliance with Decree 13/2023/ND-CP, citizen telephone numbers displayed on dispatch consoles are masked by default, showing only prefix and suffix digits. Viewing the unmasked telephone number requires an explicit click action that records an unalterable audit log entry containing Operator Identifier, Timestamp, Incident Identifier, and justification.

Access Scoping for Sensitive Data: Exact victim GPS locations and personal medical records, including blood types and allergies, are strictly restricted to the active dispatcher and the assigned rescue unit. Access permissions are automatically revoked once the incident is officially resolved.

Brute-Force Account Protection: Entering an incorrect password five consecutive times triggers an automatic temporary account lock for 15 minutes, along with an alert email sent to the registered address.

#### ***5.2.4 User Interface Ergonomics and Cross-Platform Conventions***

Emergency Touch Target Sizing: All interactive buttons on mobile and vehicle-mounted tablet interfaces must maintain a minimum physical touch target of 48 by 48 pixels or display points to ensure rapid and accurate one-handed operation during crisis situations.

Standardized Color Coding and Accessibility:

Severity Level 1: Emerald Green, representing minor or developing incidents.

Severity Level 2: Amber Orange, representing moderate structural or vehicle incidents.

Severity Level 3: Crimson Red, representing critical disasters, structural fires, or mass casualty events.

Severity Level 0: Purple and Yellow warning badges, representing unclassified or artificial intelligence review-required incidents. All status badges must pair distinct colors with representative icons to assist color-blind dispatchers.

Bilingual Support: All client screens must provide native runtime language switching between Vietnamese as primary and English as secondary.

#### ***5.2.5 Data Persistence, Soft Deletion, and Auditability***

Universal Soft Deletion Rule: In compliance with Business Rule 35, critical domain records including Users, Stations, Rescue Units, Incidents, and Mission Assignments must never be physically deleted from the database. Deletions are executed exclusively via boolean soft-delete flags and recorded deletion timestamps.

Standard Audit Tracking: Every transactional entity table in the database must inherit standard auditing columns, including Creation Timestamp, Created By User Identifier, Update Timestamp, and Updated By User Identifier.

Concurrency Protection: Core operational entities implement optimistic concurrency row version tokens to prevent race conditions when multiple operators attempt to assign units to the same incident simultaneously.

#### ***5.2.6 Fault Tolerance and Offline Capability***

Client-Side Offline Queue: In cases of temporary mobile network disruption, emergency SOS reports are saved to secure local device storage and automatically retried using exponential backoff intervals of 2 seconds, 4 seconds, 8 seconds, and 16 seconds once network connectivity is restored.

Resilient Integration Policies: External dependencies, such as Cloudinary media uploads, Firebase push notifications, and Vision-Language AI inference, are governed by automated retry policies featuring a 20-second timeout, 3 exponential retry attempts, and a 30-second circuit breaker upon encountering 5 consecutive failures.

## **1\. System Design** {#1.-system-design}

## **1\. System Design**

### **1.1 System Architecture**

![][image34]

***Figure 113 \- System Architecture Diagram*** 

***System Architecture Diagram Description*** 

| No | Component | Description |
| :---: | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | **Client Side** | The client side represents the user-facing part of the system, including the web application and mobile application. It is responsible for displaying interfaces, handling user interactions, updating UI data, and sending requests to the server side. |
| **2** | **Web App** | The web application is used by users through a browser. It follows the MVP pattern, including View, Presenter, and Model, to separate UI rendering, user interaction handling, and data management. It provides full dispatching capabilities for operators, worker reporting, and exclusive administrative management. |
| **3** | **Mobile App** | The mobile application provides system functions for mobile users (on-site workers and quick response teams). It follows the MVVM pattern, including View, View Model, Model, and Coordinator, to manage UI rendering, business state, data updates, and screen navigation. |
| **4** | **View** | The view is responsible for displaying the user interface and receiving user actions. It does not directly handle business logic but forwards events to the presenter (Web App) or view model (Mobile App). |
| **5** | **Presenter** | The presenter acts as an intermediary between the view and the model in the web application. It receives user actions from the view, processes logic, invokes services, updates the model, and sends updated data back to the view. |
| **6** | **Model** | The model stores and manages application data on the client side. It is updated when data changes and provides data back to the presenter or view model for UI updates. |
| **7** | **Coordinator** | The coordinator manages screen flow and navigation hierarchy in the mobile application. It handles deep linking, such as navigating directly from an incoming emergency siren notification to the live campus map route. |
| **8** | **View Model** | The view model encapsulates the presentation logic and state for the mobile views. It transforms domain data into view-friendly format, handles user input, and manages background tasks such as periodic vehicle GPS telemetry transmission. |
| **9** | **Web socket** | The WebSocket component (implemented via SignalR) establishes a persistent, full-duplex communication channel between client applications and the backend. It enables sub-second broadcasting of live vehicle GPS coordinates and real-time CAD queue updates. |
| **10** | **Send / Return HTTP Request** | Represents the standard stateless RESTful communication over HTTPS. Clients send HTTP requests (e.g., incident submission, user login, dispatch verification), and the server returns structured JSON responses (ApiResponseDto\<T\>). |
| **11** | **Server Side** | The server side represents the central hosting environment containing the backend application logic and the database. It processes incoming client requests, executes core dispatch algorithms, communicates with external cloud services, and maintains data persistence. |
| **12** | **Back-end** | The core application software built on ASP.NET Core 9.0 following Clean Architecture principles. It isolates enterprise business rules from external frameworks, infrastructure adapters, and database engines. |
| **13** | **API Layer (REST API)** | The outermost layer of the backend, containing RESTful Controllers, JWT Bearer authentication, request validation (FluentValidation), and the Escalation Background Worker which periodically checks for unresolved critical incidents. |
| **14** | **Application Layer** | The orchestration layer contains core business logic, application services, DTOs, and the **Dispatch Recommendation Engine**. It calculates optimal unit assignments within campus geofences using *Nearest-Available* and *Load-Aware* algorithms. |
| **15** | **Domain Layer** | The central core of the system contains enterprise entities (Incident, RescueUnit, Station, DispatchAssignment, IncidentAuditTrail), status enumerations, and repository interfaces without any external dependencies. |
| **16** | **Infrastructure Layer** | The layer responsible for external technical concerns, divided into **Persistence** (data access implementation) and **Infrastructure Services** (adapters for third-party cloud integrations). |
| **17** | **Infrastructure Services** | Houses adapters that encapsulate external cloud integrations, including the AI classification adapter (Qwen-VL), media upload adapter (Cloudinary), push notification adapter (FCM), and SMTP email adapter. |
| **18** | **Persistence** | Implements the domain repository interfaces using Entity Framework Core 9 (Npgsql). It translates high-level domain operations into relational SQL queries, manages migrations, and handles spatial PostGIS operations. |
| **19** | **Database** | The centralized relational database is powered by PostgreSQL (hosted on Neon Cloud) with PostGIS extensions. It stores user credentials, security stations, patrol units, geofenced boundaries, and immutable audit logs. |
| **20** | **3rd Party Service** | The external cloud infrastructure layer provides auxiliary capabilities (storage, mapping, push notification, AI, and authentication) consumed by both client applications and the backend server. |
| **21** | **OAuth Service** | External authentication provider (Google OAuth 2.0) that verifies identity tokens, enabling single sign-on (SSO) for authorized enterprise personnel and workers. |
| **22** | **Store Service** | Cloud object storage (Cloudinary CDN) dedicated to receiving, storing, transforming, and delivering incident evidence photos/videos and post-incident resolution reports over HTTPS. |
| **23** | **Notification Service** | Cloud messaging service (Firebase Cloud Messaging \- FCM) responsible for sending high-priority alerts with custom audible siren sounds to on-duty response teams, even when screens are locked. |
| **24** | **Map Service** | Digital mapping and routing engine (OSRM / Mapbox) that serves digitized campus road tiles to client views and computes accurate driving distance and ETA matrices for dispatch calculations. |
| **25** | **Cache Service** | In-memory caching layer (Memory / Redis) utilized to store active user sessions, vehicle availability flags, and frequently queried spatial data to reduce database load. |
| **26** | **Check Image Service** | Vision-Language AI model (Qwen-VL) that inspects uploaded incident images to extract industrial hazard tags (fire, toxic smoke, chemical leaks) and compute severity scores (Level 1–3). |
| **27** | **Email Service** | SMTP mail transfer agent (Gmail SMTP) responsible for delivering registration OTP verification codes, welcome instructions, and real-time security alerts upon password change. |

#### ***1.2.3 Backend***

![][image37]

**Figure 117 – Package Diagram \- Backend** 

***Package Descriptions***

| No | Package | Layer | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Controllers | API | Contains RESTful API endpoints responsible for handling incoming HTTP requests, invoking application services, and returning responses to clients. |
| 2 | Hubs (SignalR) | API | Contains SignalR endpoints for handling real-time, bi-directional communication with clients (e.g., live ambulance tracking, emergency alerts). |
| 3 | Middlewares | API | Includes custom components that handle cross-cutting concerns such as global exception handling, request logging, and JWT authentication before requests reach controllers. |
| 4 | DTOs | Application | (Data Transfer Objects) Objects used specifically to encapsulate data for API requests and responses, ensuring the database schema is hidden from the client. |
| 5 | Validators | Application | Contains validation rules (e.g., FluentValidation) to ensure the integrity and correctness of incoming DTOs before they are processed by business logic. |
| 6 | Interfaces (IService) | Application | Defines contracts/interfaces for application services. This allows the API layer to interact with business logic without knowing its concrete implementation. |
| 7 | Services | Application | Contains the concrete implementations of application business logic, orchestrating use cases such as dispatching ambulances or processing incidents. |
| 8 | Models | Application | Internal data models and structures used strictly within the application logic for temporary data transformations or calculations. |
| 9 | Helper | Application | Utility classes and static methods for common, reusable tasks across the application (e.g., coordinate distance calculation, formatting). |
| 10 | Entities | Domain | Represents the core business objects (e.g., Incident, Ambulance, User) that are central to the domain logic. These classes map directly to database tables. |
| 11 | Enums | Domain | Contains sets of named constants used to represent fixed categories or states across the system (e.g., IncidentStatus, AmbulanceStatus). |
| 12 | Exceptions | Domain | Custom exception classes representing domain-specific business logic violations and application-level failures (e.g., AmbulanceUnavailableException). |
| 13 | Interfaces (IRepository) | Domain | Interface definitions for data access, following the Repository pattern. They dictate what data operations are allowed without exposing database technologies. |
| 14 | Data (Context) | Infrastructure | Contains the database context (e.g., EF Core ApplicationDbContext) responsible for managing database connections, entity mapping, and tracking changes. |
| 15 | Migrations | Infrastructure | Auto-generated Entity Framework files used to keep track of database schema changes and apply updates incrementally to the PostgreSQL database. |
| 16 | Repositories | Infrastructure | Concrete implementations of the IRepository interfaces. This package handles direct data persistence and querying via Entity Framework Core. |
| 17 | ExternalServices | Infrastructure | Implementations of services that interact with external third-party providers (e.g., AI integration, Email SMTP, Cloudinary image upload). |
| 18 | Configuration | Infrastructure | Contains classes for reading setup values, managing environment variables, and configuring external libraries. |
| 19 | BackgroundServices | Infrastructure | Implementations of hosted services used for executing long-running background tasks and periodic operations (e.g., cleanup jobs, timeout checks). |

# **V. Software Testing Documentation**

## **1\. Scope of Testing**

### **1.1. In-Scope**

Web CAD Dashboard & Admin Portal: Testing of the digitized GIS campus map interface, the CAD priority queue (prioritizing Level 0 and Level 3 incidents), and the incident verification mechanism (a "human-in-the-loop" process for confirming incidents, overriding severity levels, or canceling erroneous entries). This also includes testing the dispatch recommendation engine (comparing "Nearest-Available" vs. "Load-Aware" allocation strategies), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and an immutable incident audit trail.

Mobile Applications (Worker App & QRT Rescuer App): Cross-platform testing (iOS & Android) for features such as one-tap SOS alerts with GPS coordinates, on-site photo/video capture, indoor campus navigation, continuous GPS tracking of patrol vehicles, and the generation of shift-closure reports, including verification photos.

Comprehensive evaluation of the in-house fine-tuned Vision-Language model (Custom Qwen2.5-VL) deployed on a dedicated GPU inference server (vLLM / FastAPI). Key validations include:

• Multi-label hazard classification accuracy on High-Tech Park industrial emergency imagery (\#Fire, \#Accident, \#Traffic\_Jam).

• Objective severity scoring alignment (Level 1 to Level 3 / Level 5).

• Vietnamese incident contextual summary generation quality.

• Model resilience and fallback handling under heavy concurrent GPU workload.

Real-time WebSocket & Notification Layer: Testing of the SignalR WebSocket Hub (/hubs/dispatch) for transmitting rescue vehicle GPS coordinates with a latency of under 1 second, including automated incident queue synchronization and the delivery of high-priority emergency alerts—featuring a siren sound—via FCM HTTP v1 to mobile devices, even when the screen is locked.

REST API Gateway & Security: Comprehensive testing of all HTTP endpoints, including JWT Bearer authentication, refresh token mechanisms, Single Sign-On (SSO) via Google OAuth 2.0, and input data integrity validation (using FluentValidation).

### **1.2. Out-Scope**

Integration with external public emergency services (such as 114 or 115\) is not tested, as the system’s scope has been narrowed to focus exclusively on the enclosed premises of the High-Tech Park.

Physical IoT sensor hardware, production lines, and electronic actuators on patrol vehicles are not tested.

Financial payment gateways and commercial invoicing systems are excluded.

### **1.3. Assumptions and Constraints**

Network Connectivity: All mobile devices and Web Client workstations must operate within an environment with stable campus Wi-Fi or 4G/5G coverage.

Media Constraints: File uploads to Cloudinary are strictly limited: a maximum of 10 MB for images (JPEG, PNG, WEBP) and 30 MB for videos (MP4, MOV).

AI Timeout Constraint: The response time for AI models via OpenRouter is capped at 25 seconds. If this limit is exceeded, a circuit breaker is triggered, activating "Fallback Level 0" (Unclassified).

## Geofencing Constraint: All submitted GPS coordinates are cross-referenced against the PostGIS boundary polygon of the High-Tech Park; any coordinates falling outside this area will be flagged with a warning.

## **2\. Test Strategy**

*\[List out and describe all testing types (you can refer the test types listed below or any other test types to selected the suitable ones for the project; for each selected test types you need to provide the following information: test objective, technique, completion criteria, etc.), test levels that those test types would be performed, & the details of test supporting tools would be used in the project\]*

### **2.1 Testing Types**

The mobile client tier (Emergency Dispatch Mobile Client) is engineered using React Native 0.86 (Expo 57\) and TypeScript, deeply integrating on-device hardware capabilities (GPS Sensor via expo-location, Camera/Media Library via expo-image-picker, Digital Mapping via Mapbox GL / WebView, and Local Persistence via @react-native-async-storage/async-storage). It interfaces with backend services via a RESTful Web API (.NET 9.0 Clean Architecture), Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM), and a dual-tier AI pipeline (YOLO for on-scene hazard detection and Qwen Vision-Language for contextual severity classification).

The system manages 3 specific incident categories: Fire, Traffic Accident, and Traffic Congestion. Traffic Congestion serves as an auxiliary informational alert without severity grading, whereas Fire and Accident incidents undergo multi-level severity classification to mobilize specialized emergency response units.

#### ***2.1.1. Functional Testing***

Objective: Verify the behavioral correctness of all mission-critical user workflows for both Citizens and Field Workers / Responders according to the Software Requirements Specification (SRS). Core functionalities include: initiating emergency SOS alarms, capturing and uploading on-scene media (photos/videos), reverse-geocoding GPS coordinates into human-readable street addresses, submitting auxiliary traffic congestion reports, tracking real-time vehicle locations and estimated time of arrival (ETA), and receiving AI processing results (YOLO detects visual entities such as flames, smoke, damaged vehicles, and road obstacles; Qwen Vision-Language classifies severity levels for Fire and Accident emergencies, while Traffic Congestion is recorded as an unranked auxiliary notice).

\- Technique:

  \+ Black-box Testing: Verifying functionality against end-to-end user operational scenarios without inspecting internal state.

  \+ Equivalence Partitioning: Segmenting input domains into valid and invalid classes (e.g., valid coordinates vs. null/out-of-bounds coordinates; image file size \<= 10MB vs. \> 10MB).

  \+ Boundary Value Analysis: Testing behavioral thresholds (e.g., SOS hold duration: 1.9s does not trigger, \>= 2.0s triggers camera immediately; maximum text note length).

  \+ Decision Table Testing: Validating combinatorial logic for the 3 distinct incident categories (Fire and Traffic Accident with severity levels, and Traffic Congestion without severity grading).

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ 100% of Critical and High priority functional test cases are executed with a Pass status.

  \+ Zero unresolved Blocker, Critical, or Major defects impacting SOS signaling, incident creation, or map visualization.

  \+ Traffic Congestion reports display correctly as unranked auxiliary alerts without severity score, while Fire and Accident incidents correctly display their classified severity badges.

  \+ All error conditions and peripheral states (e.g., camera permission denied, location disabled) gracefully present actionable user guidance.  
**2.1.2. UI/UX & Responsive Testing**

 Objective: Ensure that the user interface maintains strict visual consistency, adheres to the defined Design System tokens, and seamlessly adapts across heterogeneous screen viewports (ranging from compact displays \< 375px to large displays \> 430px). Ensure comprehensive support for hardware safe areas (display cutouts, notch, Dynamic Island, and Android virtual navigation bars). Crucial touch targets (SOS Pulse button, capture shutter, 114/115 speed-dial buttons) must strictly reside within the ergonomic thumb-reach zone.

\- Technique:

  \+ Visual Inspection: Comparing pixel rendering against Figma UI/UX design specifications across diverse aspect ratios (16:9 to 20:9).

  \+ Dynamic Metric Scaling: Validating layout responsiveness utilizing react-native-size-matters and the custom useResponsive hook (moderateScale, fontScale, isSmallDevice).

  \+ Orientation Constraint: Enforcing fixed portrait orientation to prevent accidental UI disorientations during distress situations.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ Zero uncontrolled text clippings, overlapping components, or obscured primary action buttons across all target screen densities.

  \+ Bottom sheets and dialog modals (MediaReportModal, SosSuccessModal, StaffNotificationsModal) render within viewport boundaries and support smooth gesture dismissals.

#### ***2.1.3. Usability & Accessibility Testing***

 Objective: Guarantee that under extreme stress and panic, citizens can successfully transmit an emergency SOS beacon within 3 seconds using minimal intuitive interactions. Ensure high visual contrast, clear haptic/vibration sensory feedback, and full compliance with assistive screen readers for visually impaired users.

\- Technique:

  \+ User Journey Simulation: Measuring cognitive friction, interaction steps, and elapsed time from app cold launch to successful SOS broadcast.

  \+ Haptic Feedback Verification: Validating urgent rhythmic vibration patterns (Vibration.vibrate(\[0, 250, 100, 250\])) upon emergency trigger.

  \+ Accessibility Audit: Inspecting accessibility attributes (accessible=true, accessibilityLabel, accessibilityRole='button') across interactive elements.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ First-time users successfully dispatch an emergency alarm within \<= 3 seconds without prior training or reference manual.

  \+ Assistive screen readers (TalkBack on Android, VoiceOver on iOS) accurately announce the SOS button state and resolved current address.

#### ***2.1.4. Network Simulation & Offline Resilience Testing***

 Objective: Validate the client application's resilience and data integrity under adverse network conditions (cellular blackouts, Wi-Fi to 4G handover, Airplane mode, high packet loss, and throttled bandwidth). Specifically verify the client-side Offline Queue mechanism via @react-native-async-storage/async-storage and automated Retry & Synchronization once connectivity is restored, preventing data loss or duplicate incident creation.

\- Technique:

  \+ Network Throttling: Simulating degraded profiles (Offline, High Latency 2000ms, Packet Loss 20%, Throttled 3G).

  \+ Sudden State Transition Testing: Switching connectivity states (Online \-\> Offline \-\> Online) mid-submission.

  \+ Idempotency Verification: Ensuring queued incidents flush exactly once without generating duplicate database records.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ The application does not freeze, crash, or show an unhandled blank screen upon abrupt connection loss.

  \+ SOS requests created while offline are securely cached locally and automatically synchronized with the backend server within 5 seconds of network restoration.

#### ***2.1.5. Security & Device Permission Testing***

\- Objective: Ensure that hardware runtime permissions (Foreground Location, Camera, Photo Library, and Push Notifications) conform strictly to Android and iOS platform security standards. Validate secure storage of JWT Access/Refresh tokens and guarantee that sensitive health profile data (blood type, medical history, emergency contacts) remain encrypted in transit and protected against unauthorized leakage.

\- Technique:

  \+ Permission Grant/Revocation Matrix: Testing application behavior across Granted, Denied, and 'Never Ask Again' permission states.

  \+ Token Refresh Flow: Validating automated silent token refresh cycles via /api/auth/refresh through Axios interceptors.

  \+ Log & Transport Leakage Inspection: Verifying that JWT tokens, passwords, and PII are never emitted to production release logs or unencrypted HTTP channels.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ Denial of camera or location permissions displays informative dialogs prompting navigation to system settings rather than crashing.

  \+ All outbound network communication is enforced over HTTPS/TLS with proper Authorization: Bearer \<token\> headers.

####  ***2.1.6. Performance & Battery Consumption Testing***

\- Objective: Measure cold/warm launch latency, frame rate stability during complex map interactions (pan, zoom, multi-marker rendering via Mapbox), media compression and upload throughput, RAM footprint, and battery drain associated with continuous GPS polling.

\- Technique:

  \+ Profiling: Tracking CPU and memory allocation using Android Studio Profiler and Xcode Instruments.

  \+ Frame Rate Monitoring: Benchmarking UI rendering thread to ensure consistent 60 FPS across interactive animations.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ Rendering performance sustains \>= 55 \- 60 FPS during normal map interactions and bottom-sheet dragging.

  \+ On-scene image compression and Cloudinary upload completes within \<= 3.5 seconds over standard 4G networks.

  \+ App memory consumption remains below 250 MB during active map navigation sessions.

#### ***2.1.7. . Functional UI Testing (Web Command Center Dashboard)***

\- Objective: Verify that every Operator workflow on the dashboard behaves correctly. This covers the CAD Live Map (incidents in the Fire and Accident branches color-coded by severity Level 1–3, vehicle and fixed-station positions, traffic-jam markers, marker clustering, drag-and-drop of a vehicle onto an incident); the priority queue (Level 3 first, then Level 2, then Level 1, with FIFO ordering inside the same level; traffic-jam reports shown without a severity level); the 2-minute soft lock when an Operator opens a case; the Human-in-the-Loop AI verification panel (media shown side by side with AI event type, level, confidence % and hazard tags; confirm or override with a mandatory reason of at least 5 characters written to IncidentAuditTrail; masked phone number with an audited "Show number" action; cancellation of false reports and blacklisting in BlockedPhoneNumberList for 7 days / 30 days / 1 year / permanently); the dispatch recommendation panel (vehicle type matched to incident type, Nearest-Available vs. Load-Aware ranking, automatic radius expansion 10 → 15 → 22.5 → 30 km, 1-click assignment, selection of 2–5 vehicles for Level 3); and the escalation alarm (red border and alert on the whole dashboard).

\- Technique:

  \+ Scenario-based Black-box Testing: Executing end-to-end Operator scenarios (receive incident → open case → verify/override AI result → dispatch → monitor → close) against the expected business behavior without inspecting internal code.

  \+ Equivalence Partitioning & Boundary Value Analysis: Override reason of 4 characters (rejected) vs. 5 characters (accepted); number of vehicles for a Level 3 incident at 1, 2, 5 and 6; soft lock released at 1:59 vs. 2:00; escalation triggered at 4:59 vs. 5:00 by day and at 2:29 vs. 2:30 at night (22:00–06:00), including the 21:59 / 22:00 and 05:59 / 06:00 switch-over points.

  \+ Decision Table Testing: Combinations of incident branch (Fire / Accident / Traffic Jam) × severity level (1–3) × vehicle type (fire truck / ambulance) × vehicle status (Available / OnMission / Recovery / Maintenance) to check which vehicles are suggested and which are blocked.

  \+ State Transition Testing: Validating that the UI only offers legal transitions of an incident (Pending → Verified → Dispatched → EnRoute → OnScene → Resolved, plus Cancelled and Escalated) and of a vehicle, and that a multi-vehicle case only closes when every assigned vehicle has submitted its report.

  \+ Concurrency Testing: Two Operator sessions opening the same case or assigning the same vehicle at the same time; the second action must be refused (soft lock / RowVersion conflict, HTTP 409\) with a clear message.

  \+ Role-Based Access Checks: Logging in as Operator, Admin, RescueStaff and Citizen to confirm that only authorized roles can open the dashboard and each action (override, blacklist, show phone number) is visible only to permitted roles.

  \+ Automated UI Regression: Re-running the critical Operator scenarios as browser automation scripts (e.g. Playwright) after every build.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ 100% of Critical and High priority dashboard test cases are executed with a Pass status, and at least 95% of all dashboard test cases pass.

  \+ Zero open Blocker, Critical or Major defects on queue ordering, soft lock / concurrency, AI override, dispatch assignment or escalation alarm.

  \+ Every override, "Show number" action and cancellation produces exactly one matching record in the immutable audit trail.

  \+ Every validation error (short override reason, wrong vehicle type, locked case, 409 conflict) shows a clear message and leaves the screen in a consistent state.

#### **2.1.8. WebSocket Real-time Testing (SignalR Hub)**

\- Objective: Verify that the dashboard receives and displays real-time data from the SignalR Core hub (/hubs/dispatch, per-incident groups incident\_{id}) correctly, quickly and reliably. Events in scope: new incident pushed into the queue, incident status changes, vehicle GPS updates every 3–5 seconds, soft lock / unlock notifications between Operators, rescue team Accept/Reject responses, and escalation broadcasts. Performance targets: GPS latency through SignalR \< 500 ms, dashboard synchronization within 1–3 seconds, and at least 200 concurrent WebSocket connections.

\- Technique:

  \+ Multi-client Event Verification: Running several Operator browsers together with the mobile Staff/Citizen apps (or simulated clients) and checking that one action is reflected on all subscribed screens, in the correct order and exactly once.

  \+ Latency Measurement: Comparing the server send timestamp with the time each update is rendered on the dashboard over at least 500 GPS messages, and reporting average, p95 and maximum latency.

  \+ Connection Resilience Testing: Cutting the network with browser DevTools (Offline / slow 3G), switching Wi-Fi, putting the laptop to sleep and restarting the backend container mid-session, then checking automatic reconnection with back-off, a visible connection-status indicator, and re-synchronization of the queue and vehicle positions through REST after reconnecting.

  \+ Hub Security Testing: Connecting without a token, with an expired JWT and with a non-Operator role; verifying that the connection is refused and that a client cannot join an incident\_{id} group it is not authorized for. Confirming the connection uses WSS only.

  \+ Load & Soak Testing: Opening 200 concurrent hub connections with simulated vehicles sending GPS every 3 seconds (e.g. k6 or a custom SignalR client script) and running a 30-minute soak session while monitoring dropped connections, memory growth and UI frame rate on the dashboard.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ p95 GPS update latency \< 500 ms and no single update above 1 second under normal load.

  \+ Incident and status changes appear on every subscribed dashboard within 3 seconds.

  \+ After a connection loss the dashboard reconnects automatically within 5 seconds of network recovery and shows the correct queue and vehicle positions with no lost or duplicated events.

  \+ 200 concurrent connections are sustained for 30 minutes with no unexpected disconnections and no noticeable UI freeze.

  \+ Unauthenticated or unauthorized hub connections are rejected in 100% of test cases.

#### **2.1.9. Cross-browser & Responsive Compatibility Testing (Web)**

\- Objective: Ensure the dashboard works and looks consistent on the target browsers (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Apple Safari and Microsoft Edge, latest two stable versions) and across three screen breakpoints: \> 1024 px (desktop layout with 65% map / 35% queue), 600–1024 px (tablet layout with the queue in a Bottom Sheet) and \< 600 px (minimum supported view). Browser-specific features that must be checked: WebGL map rendering, WebSocket transport (and SignalR fallback to Server-Sent Events / Long Polling when WebSockets are blocked), Web Push and Notification API permissions, audio alarm playback under each browser's autoplay policy, IndexedDB caching, and drag-and-drop on mouse and touch screens.

\- Technique:

  \+ Compatibility Matrix Testing: Running the same set of critical dashboard test cases on every browser × operating system pair (Windows 10/11: Chrome, Edge, Firefox; macOS: Safari, Chrome) and recording Pass/Fail per cell.

  \+ Automated Multi-engine Execution: Running the automated UI scripts on the Chromium, Firefox and WebKit engines, with manual confirmation on real Safari for Web Push and audio behavior.

  \+ Responsive Layout Inspection: Checking the layout at 1920×1080, 1366×768, 1024×768, 768×1024 and 390×844 viewports with browser DevTools and comparing screenshots with the Figma designs.

  \+ Front-end Performance Audit: Measuring First Contentful Paint and Live Map load time with Lighthouse / DevTools Performance on each browser using a dataset of 100 vehicles and 50 incidents.

\- Completion Criteria:

  \+ All Critical and High priority dashboard test cases pass on all four target browsers; any remaining Minor cosmetic difference is documented.

  \+ No overlapping, clipped or hidden primary controls (queue, verify/override, dispatch buttons) at any of the three breakpoints.

  \+ Real-time updates, alarm sound and browser notifications work on every target browser, including when SignalR falls back from WebSockets.

  \+ First Contentful Paint ≤ 1.5 seconds and Live Map load with 100 vehicles \+ 50 incidents \< 2.0 seconds on the reference workstation in every target browser.

#### **2.1.10. Backend REST API & Integration Testing**

\- Objective: Verify contract fidelity, transaction isolation, error-handling semantics, and seamless integration between the .NET 9 Clean Architecture Web API, Neon Serverless PostgreSQL (with PostGIS spatial extensions), Cloudinary media CDN, and the asynchronous AI processing pipeline.

\- Technique:

* API Contract Testing: Validating request/response DTO schemas against Swagger/OpenAPI 3.0 specifications using Postman runner collections.  
* Transactional Integrity Verification: Ensuring atomic database rollbacks (Unit of Work pattern) upon unexpected runtime exceptions during complex multi-table mutations (e.g., incident creation with media records and audit history).  
* Multipart Ingestion Testing: Verifying concurrent multipart/form-data upload streams containing GPS coordinates, reporter metadata, and high-resolution JPEG/PNG images or MP4 videos routed to Cloudinary.  
* Channel Queue Backpressure Verification: Validating that incoming incidents are reliably written to IAiAnalysisQueue (in-memory bounded channel) without dropping items under load.

\- Completion Criteria:

* 100% of REST API endpoints return documented HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500).  
* Zero orphan records in PostgreSQL tables following simulated failure midway through incident submission.  
* All image and video uploads to Cloudinary succeed and store immutable secure HTTPS URLs in the database.

#### ***2.1.11. Performance Testing (SLA & Latency Benchmarks)***

\- Objective: Benchmark server-side processing latency, database query execution times, and throughput (Requests Per Second \- RPS) under steady-state baseline and peak operating loads. Ensure system meets GovTech real-time emergency SLAs.

\- Technique:

* Scripted Load Testing via k6: Simulating stepped virtual users (20 VUs baseline, 100 VUs regular, 200 VUs peak load) over 5-minute sustained durations.  
* Percentile Profiling: Measuring Average, 90th percentile (p90), and 95th percentile (p95) latency profiles across high-frequency endpoints (\`GET /api/incidents\`, \`GET /api/stations/nearby\`, \`POST /api/incidents\`).  
* Database Connection Pool Profiling: Monitoring PostgreSQL serverless connection pool usage, active thread pool workers, and query latency via Neon console and pgAdmin.

\- Completion Criteria:

* \>= 95% of standard query/read REST API requests complete within \< 300 ms (Actual benchmark: 184 ms at 100 CCU).  
* End-to-end incident ingestion (\`POST /api/incidents\` with media upload & channel dispatch) p95 response time is \< 1,500 ms (Actual: 1,320 ms).  
* Total HTTP 5xx error rate remains strictly \< 0.5% during sustained peak load.

#### ***2.1.12. Stress & Concurrency Testing (Spike Load & Queue Saturation)***

\- Objective: Identify architectural breaking points, verify system resilience against sudden surge traffic (e.g., major industrial disaster or park-wide chemical leak), and confirm graceful degradation under extreme resource contention.

\- Technique:

* Extreme Concurrency Spike via Apache JMeter: Blasting 200 to 500 concurrent virtual users within a 10-second burst against incident submission endpoints.  
* Queue Saturation & Memory Profiling: Stressing the in-memory bounded channel (IAiAnalysisQueue) up to 1,000 pending items; verifying that AiAnalysisWorker and EscalationWorker process tasks FIFO without memory leaks or OutOfMemory exceptions.  
* Chaos & Fault Injection: Terminating the local GPU AI microservice during peak load to verify automatic Polly Circuit Breaker tripping and seamless fallback to OpenRouter Cloud API.

\- Completion Criteria:

* Zero unhandled application crashes or fatal process terminations.  
* AI pipeline circuit breaker trips upon GPU microservice unavailability and transparently routes requests to Cloud AI within \< 2.0 seconds without dropping a single SOS report.  
* Server returns HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) or gracefully queues requests when threshold is exceeded, recovering to normal latency within 30 seconds after traffic normalizes.

**2.1.13. Network Latency & End-to-End Real-Time Synchronization Testing (1–3s SLA)**

\- Objective: Verify that emergency SOS notifications and vehicle GPS location streams synchronize across distributed clients within the mandatory 1–3 seconds window over WebSocket (WSS/SignalR).

\- Technique:

* Automated High-Frequency SignalR Benchmarking: Utilizing a dedicated .NET console test client emitting GPS coordinate pings at 1 ping / 3 seconds across 50 simulated active rescue units.  
* Network Degradation Profiling via Chrome DevTools: Emulating Fast 3G (1.6 Mbps down, 750 kbps up, 150 ms RTT), Slow 4G (4 Mbps down, 3 Mbps up, 80 ms RTT), and simulated 2%–5% packet loss on receiver clients.  
* Triangulated Timestamp Logging: Recording exact millisecond timestamps: T\_emit (Rescue vehicle transmits coordinate) \-\> T\_hub (SignalR Hub ingests) \-\> T\_received (Dispatcher Web Map renders pin).

\- Completion Criteria:

* End-to-End Real-Time Latency: Delta\_T \= T\_received \- T\_emit \<= 3,000 ms across 100% of successful transmissions (Target SLA: 1,000 ms – 2,500 ms; Actual benchmark average: 1,240 ms).  
* SignalR connection automatically re-establishes (withAutomaticReconnect) within 5 seconds upon temporary connection interruption without requiring page reload.  
* Zero out-of-order coordinate rendering or duplicate markers on the Dispatcher Leaflet live map.

#### ***2.1.14. Security, Access Control (RBAC) & Data Privacy Testing (PII & Decree 13/2023/ND-CP)***

\- Objective: Ensure strict enforcement of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), verify cryptographic transport security, and protect sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and emergency medical data in compliance with Vietnam legal standards.

\- Technique:

* RBAC Penetration Simulation: Generating forged and legitimate JWT tokens for Citizen and RescueStaff roles, attempting horizontal and vertical privilege escalation against restricted endpoints (PUT /api/incidents/{id}/verify, POST /api/users, /api/stations).  
* Transport Cryptography Inspection: Validating TLS 1.3 / HTTPS encryption, WSS enforcement, and password hashing strength using BCrypt (work factor 11).  
* PII Masking & Privacy Audit (Decree 13/2023/ND-CP): Verifying that citizen phone numbers are masked (09\*\*\*\*1234), National IDs (CCCD) are concealed from non-admin roles, and medical profiles (blood type, allergies) remain locked (HTTP 403\) outside of active emergency dispatch missions.  
* Token Invalidation & Session Revocation: Verifying that password changes or explicit logout immediately revokes the active Refresh Token and rejects subsequent access (HTTP 401 Unauthorized).

\- Completion Criteria:

* 100% of unauthorized endpoint invocations return HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden with localized error messages.  
* Zero cleartext passwords or unhashed secrets stored in the database or transmitted across network interfaces.  
* Citizen PII is securely masked in public queues, fully satisfying Vietnam Decree 13/2023/ND-CP compliance.

#### ***2.1.15. Bilingual & Localization Verification (vi / en)***

\- Objective: Confirm that backend response messages and validation errors adapt seamlessly to the user's selected language (vi vs. en).

\- Technique:

* Sending requests with varying Accept-Language headers (vi, en, vi-VN, en-US), query parameters (?culture=en), and default headers.

\- Completion Criteria:

* When Accept-Language: en is present, 100% of ApiResponseDto.Message and Errors display grammatically accurate English text.  
* Default behavior falls back reliably to Vietnamese (vi).

### **Description of Test Levels**

1\. Unit Testing: Verifies the correctness of individual functions, methods, logical expressions, and domain entities in isolation:

  \- Mobile Client: location.service.ts, mapbox.service.ts, asyncStorage.ts, and Zustand stores (useLocationStore, useAppStore).

  \- Backend: Domain entity validation, enum parsing, utility helpers (LocalizationCatalog), and repository mocks using xUnit.net and Moq.

2\. Integration Testing: Verifies interactions between subsystem modules, third-party infrastructure, and network protocols:

 \- Mobile Integration: Device hardware interfaces (GPS via expo-location, Camera via expo-image-picker, offline storage via AsyncStorage).

   \- API & Service Integration: RESTful API controllers with Neon Serverless PostgreSQL (PostGIS geofencing queries), Cloudinary CDN multipart upload pipeline, and SignalR Core WebSocket hubs (/hubs/dispatch, /hubs/tracking, /hubs/incidents).

   \- AI Microservice Integration: Communication between backend channel worker and local FastAPI Qwen2.5-VL LoRA GPU server, with Polly circuit breaker fallback to OpenRouter Cloud API.

3\. System Testing: Tests the complete end-to-end emergency response lifecycle in an integrated staging environment:

   \- Incident lifecycle from citizen 1-tap SOS trigger \-\> Cloudinary image upload \-\> AI triage \-\> Operator CAD verification \-\> Dispatch recommendation \-\> Field responder navigation \-\> Closure report submission.

   \- Non-functional system validation: k6 load testing under 100 CCU, JMeter 500 CCU spike testing, SignalR 1–3s GPS synchronization SLA, and 1-hour endurance testing.

4\. Acceptance Testing (UAT): Evaluates usability, operational ergonomics, regulatory compliance (Decree 13/2023/ND-CP), and business readiness under real-world High-Tech Park simulated disaster drills involving all system actor personas.
